w10_T4_003903: The school library's poetry shelf started the term with 82 books. During the first week 13 books were found damaged and were thrown away. Another 33 books were lent to a partner school and never came back. Over the holidays the librarian rebuilt the shelf, ordering 7 copies of every title still standing on it. A parent then donated 32 more poetry books to the same shelf. How many books are on the poetry shelf now?
w10_T4_003917: Devon started the month with 128 minutes on his music-practice card. He used 119 minutes preparing for an audition, then his teacher added 29 minutes as a reward and his aunt bought him 62 more. He divided the minutes then on the card equally into 5 identical daily slots and kept just one slot on his own card, passing the rest to his sister. A rescan glitch cost him 2 minutes, and the studio credited him 46 minutes for a lesson it cancelled. The studio prints these credits in hours on its noticeboard, but Devon always counts his in minutes, and half of the practice rooms were closed for painting that week. How many minutes are on Devon's card now?
w10_T4_003922: Ana's orchard had 209 apple trees, and she planted 5 more before the harvest. Every tree in the orchard filled 9 baskets. Each basket held exactly 8 apples. At the cider house every apple was cut into 2 pieces. Ana's neighbour Beto brought his own fruit and ended up with fewer pieces than Ana, so she tipped his 55 pear pieces and his 74 plum pieces into her pile as well. How many pieces are in Ana's pile now?
w10_T4_003923: On Monday morning a nursery had 50 lavender cuttings, and a supplier delivered 54 more. By noon the head grower had divided every cutting he held into 7 rooted plugs. In the afternoon a customer returned 45 plugs. During the evening market 596 plugs were sold. Overnight the propagation bench turned each plug still on site into 5 new plugs. How many plugs does the nursery have now?
w10_T4_003930: A hardware shop opened the day with 125 tins of white paint. It sold 67 tins to a decorating firm and 19 tins to walk-in customers. A cancelled order put 60 tins back on the shelf, and the afternoon delivery brought 43 more. The chain's warehouse then restocked the aisle so that the shop held 4 tins for every tin it had at that moment. Half of the aisle's shelving had just been repainted grey. How many tins of white paint does the shop hold now?
w10_T4_003933: A community radio station began its archive project with 191 tapes. Each tape was transferred into 4 separate digital tracks. The tracks were then sorted evenly into 2 equal groups, and the group of duplicates was deleted while the other group was kept. The station removed a further 267 tracks that were too noisy to broadcast. Every track that survived was cut into 5 short clips for the podcast feed, and an intern uploaded 71 extra clips found on an old hard drive. The studio clock shows recording lengths in minutes although the schedule is published in hours, and 38 volunteers are on the station's rota. How many clips are in the podcast feed now?
w10_T4_003939: Early on Saturday morning a print shop loaded 193 sheets of card into the cutter, and each sheet was cut into 8 labels. Mid-morning a customer brought 65 labels of her own to add to the tray. At lunchtime the machine reprinted the whole tray, producing 3 labels for every label present. During the afternoon 4762 labels were shipped to a supermarket. In the early evening the shop ran a final pass that made 7 copies of every label left in the tray. Just before closing, 270 labels failed the quality check and were binned. How many labels remain in the tray?
w10_T4_003943: Marisol had 72 minutes of pool time saved on her swim pass. She used 46 minutes at Tuesday's session, and her coach added 10 minutes for helping tidy the lane ropes. The centre then split what was left on her pass equally between the 4 members of her relay team, giving each member the same number of minutes. Marisol's own share was then granted to her again in each of the 6 weeks of the summer programme. The noticeboard lists pool time in hours even though passes are always issued in minutes, and half of the pool was roped off for lessons. How many minutes of pool time does Marisol get across the whole summer programme?
w10_T4_003954: Early on Monday morning a tile warehouse took in 192 pallets, and by mid-morning each pallet had been broken down into 9 cartons. In the early afternoon every carton was opened, and each one held 3 bundles of tiles. A later stock check found 71 loose bundles in the storeroom, which were added to the count. In the evening the packers unwrapped every bundle and each contained 6 tiles; the warehouse has 24 loading bays. Overnight 14827 tiles were loaded onto lorries and driven away. How many tiles are left in the warehouse?
w10_T4_003956: Theo started Saturday with 145 cents in his coin jar. He earned 78 cents washing his uncle's car and then spent 36 cents on a pencil. Later he put 120 cents towards a shared birthday present, and his sister paid back the 14 cents she had borrowed. The corner shop prices everything in dollars, but Theo keeps his savings entirely in cents, and his jar can hold up to 900 cents. How many cents are in Theo's jar at the end of the day?
w10_T4_003960: A community garden had 91 tomato plants at the start of June. A late frost killed 44 of them, and 20 more were dug up to make room for a new path. The gardeners then took cuttings until the plot held twice as many plants as it did once the path was finished. Each of those plants was later split into 9 separate pots for the summer plant sale. A neighbour donated 38 extra potted plants to the sale. How many potted plants does the sale have?
w10_T4_003963: A youth club's badge box held 22 sheets of stickers, and each sheet carried 6 badges. The leader handed out 67 badges at the first meeting of the term. A sponsor then tripled the number of badges the club still had. The badges were sorted equally into 3 identical tins, and only one tin was taken to the summer camp. At camp every badge in that tin was swapped for 5 enamel pins. How many enamel pins came back from camp?
w10_T4_003964: A school choir had 45 minutes of hall time booked, and the caretaker added 25 minutes more. The booking was split equally across the 5 weekdays, and only the Wednesday block stayed in the choir's name. A clash with the science club shortened that block by 10 minutes. The choir then held that same block in each of the 8 weeks of the autumn term, and the county trust paid for the identical programme to run in each of 7 different schools. The hall timetable is written in hours although bookings are made in minutes, and the choir has 31 members. How many minutes of hall time does the trust pay for altogether?
w10_T4_003970: A stationery wholesaler received 183 boxes of notebooks, and each box contained 9 notebooks. A returned order added 53 notebooks to the same stockroom. A school then donated 22 unused notebooks, and the local paper mill sent 57 samples. The stockroom ledger records paper weight in kilograms although the delivery notes give it in grams. How many notebooks are in the stockroom?
w10_T4_003974: Rosa and Malik run rival juice stalls, and Malik always brings fewer crates to market than Rosa does. Rosa arrived with 178 crates, and her supplier doubled that number before the market opened. She sold 120 crates during the morning. What was left was loaded equally into her 4 refrigerated vans, and from then on only the van bound for her own shop is counted. The following week the supplier doubled that van's load. The market advertises trading times in hours although the traders plan their runs in minutes. How many crates are in that van now?
w10_T4_003982: A ferry left the harbour on Monday morning carrying 134 passengers, and 42 more boarded at the first stop. At the midday stop 144 passengers went ashore. In the afternoon 47 walkers joined for the coastal run, and in the evening 69 concertgoers came aboard for the return trip. Half of the upper deck stayed closed for cleaning all day. The timetable is printed in hours, though the crew log every crossing in minutes. How many passengers are on the ferry at the end of the day?
w10_T4_003986: On Friday morning a food bank's shelf held 112 tins of soup. Volunteers took 34 tins out for the breakfast run, and a supermarket delivered 46 tins before noon. In the early afternoon a matching-gift scheme doubled the number of tins on the shelf. Later that afternoon the stock was divided equally between the charity's 4 branches, and the tins staying at the main branch are the ones being followed. In the evening 51 tins were handed out at the main branch's door. The rota is written in hours although volunteers record their shifts in minutes. How many tins are left at the main branch?
w10_T4_003996: Ines and Hugo run neighbouring seed banks, and Hugo always stores fewer sachets than Ines does. Ines started with 232 sacks of sunflower seed, and each sack filled 5 jars. Every jar was decanted into 6 packets, and every packet was then divided into 4 sachets. Damp ruined 2879 sachets, and a garden centre bought 4783 of them. Hugo handed over 55 spare sachets so that Ines could finish an order, and Ines's van can carry 900 sachets at a time. The bank weighs its stock in kilograms even though the labels are printed in grams. How many sachets does Ines have now?
w10_T4_004009: On Saturday morning Lena had 150 blank badges for the fun run, while her co-organiser Owen had fewer than she did. She used 116 badges at the early registration desk, and 7 more were ruined by the rain. At midday Owen's printer produced 5 badges for every badge Lena still held. In the afternoon a sponsor sent 33 extra badges for the box. In the evening the printer ran again, turning out 8 badges for each badge then in the box. How many badges are in the box at the end of the day?
w10_T4_004017: A city bike depot began Monday morning with 204 bikes, and 74 more came back from the repair shop before lunch. In the afternoon the council funded a replacement fleet at a rate of 4 bikes for every bike then in the depot. A dealer delivered 18 second-hand bikes in the early evening. Overnight a partner city doubled the depot's fleet as part of a swap agreement. The depot advertises its opening times in hours although hire charges are counted in minutes. How many bikes are in the depot now?
w10_T4_004023: A publisher printed 240 signatures for a new novel, and each signature folded into 6 pages. The proofreader pulled out 239 pages that were smudged, and the binder discarded 584 more that were out of order. A reprint added 27 clean pages to the stack. The publisher then bound 7 identical copies of the book, using that many pages in every single copy. The bindery keeps 12 spare sewing machines in the back room. How many pages were used across all the copies together?
w10_T4_004031: Early on Sunday morning Farah had 139 chocolates on her market stall, and her partner Jonas brought 53 more from the kitchen, which was fewer than Farah had hoped for. By late morning 73 chocolates had been sold. At lunchtime a cancelled order put 23 chocolates back on the stall. In the afternoon Farah divided the stall's chocolates equally into 2 identical boxes and took just one box on to the evening market. At the evening market a supplier matched that box exactly, so she went home with 2 boxes of that same size. How many chocolates does Farah have at the end?
w10_T4_004036: On Wednesday morning a fish market had 230 boxes of sardines. Before noon 67 boxes were sent straight to a restaurant. In the afternoon every remaining box was split into 5 trays, and by early evening each tray had been repacked into 5 small tubs. Late that evening 3414 tubs were driven to the airport. Half of the market hall was already dark by then. The auctioneer calls the sale times in hours although the porters time their runs in minutes. How many tubs are left in the market?
w10_T4_004037: A theatre started its run with 217 programmes, of which 48 were handed to the cast on opening night. The printer then delivered 78 extra programmes. For the tour the company ordered 3 programmes for every one it was holding. Over the tour 693 programmes were sold. The remainder was shared equally between the company's 2 storerooms, and the north storeroom's share was set aside for the archive. The box office quotes running times in minutes although the posters give them in hours. How many programmes went into the archive?
w10_T4_004038: A camp cook set out 14 trays of muffins, and each tray held 9 muffins. Every muffin was then cut into 4 pieces for the tasting table. The bakery van delivered 73 more pieces, a parent brought 76, and the scout troop added 73 of their own. Just before the doors opened the cook put out 35 extra pieces she had kept back in the kitchen. How many pieces are on the tasting table?
